subject: DPA: analytics carve-out and subprocessor list
messages:
From: Tom Li <tom.li@vitalbridge.com>
To: maya.srinivasan@redwood.com
Cc: Legal - VitalBridge <legal@vitalbridge.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Mar 2028 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: DPA: request for analytics carve-out and subprocessor list

Maya —

Thanks for the quick chat earlier. Attached is VitalBridge's standard DPA with our redlines (VB_DPA_v3_redline.pdf). Two asks we need clarity on before we can sign: 

1) Analytics carve-out: we are asking for a narrow carve-out to allow VitalBridge to export aggregated analytics derived from inference-level metadata (no raw PII or inference outputs). We proposed explicit language in section 4.2.

2) Subprocessors: we asked for a short, enumerated subprocessor list and the ability to add additional analytics partners with 30 days' notice (we included a sample clause).

Can Redwood Product and Security confirm whether those two items are feasible operationally and from a compliance standpoint? If not, can you propose alternative wording that would allow us to proceed?

Appreciate a response this week; our procurement timeline is tight.

Attachments: VB_DPA_v3_redline.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Tom Li
Head of Legal Operations
VitalBridge Health
From: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com
To: Tom Li <tom.li@vitalbridge.com>
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA: request for analytics carve-out and subprocessor list

Tom —

Received, thanks for sending the redline. Looping in Olga from Security and Dev from Product to weigh in on feasibility. High-level notes from my side:

- We understand VitalBridge's need for aggregated analytics; we need to confirm boundaries on what qualifies as "aggregated" and ensure no trace reconstruction is possible.
- Subprocessor additions are supported, but our standard approach is a documented allowlist + notification; we may need to push back on automatic additions with only notice.

Olga / Dev — can you review Tom's redlines (attached) and comment on alternative language we can propose to keep the deal moving?

I'll aim to consolidate proposed language and send back by EOD Monday.

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
Director, Partnerships & GTM
Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 03 Mar 2028 08:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA: request for analytics carve-out and subprocessor list

Maya / Dev —

Thanks for the ping and Tom's redline. Quick security assessment: 

- Analytics carve-out: Security is generally comfortable with an "aggregated, non-identifiable" carve-out, provided we specify sampling thresholds, aggregation windows, and exclude any export of inference outputs or raw request text. The risk vector is re-identification via correlated signals; we need explicit controls (e.g., minimum cohort size, noise injection, and no export of token-level logs).

- Subprocessors: We cannot agree to an open-ended add-by-notice for analytics partners. Our preferred model is: allowlist (current processors named in the contract) + a defined approval path for additions (e.g., we have 30 days to review and can object on security/compliance grounds). If VitalBridge requires automatic additions, we should ask Legal for compensating controls (data minimization, strict purpose limitation, and per-subprocessor attestations).

I attached a short checklist of the technical constraints I need from Product to validate implementation feasibility:
- Which telemetry fields would be in the aggregated export?
- Can we enforce cohort minimums at the runtime side?
- Any planned downstream joins that could enable re-identification?

If Dev can answer these, we can draft specific contract language.

Attachment: security_checklist_for_analytics_export.txt (text)

—Olga
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, maya_srinivasan@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 04 Mar 2028 11:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA: request for analytics carve-out and subprocessor list

Olga / Maya —

Thanks — answering the checklist and calling out implementation impacts: 

- Telemetry fields: We can provide aggregated counters (request count, latency percentiles, model variant usage) and hashed non-PII identifiers (if agreed). We cannot export raw request text or model outputs.
- Cohort enforcement: We can implement a minimum cohort size check (default 50) at the export path. That would block exports below the threshold and log the attempt. This requires a small change to the export service and a configuration flag per account (estimated 2 sprints of work: design + 1 sprint to implement + QA).
- Noise injection: We can add Laplace noise for counts as a configurable option; engineering estimate 1 sprint.
- Subprocessor workflow: We already maintain an allowlist and a 30-day review process. Automating legal approval is out of scope; we can provide an API-driven notification + a manual approval channel.

Suggested contract language (draft):
"Redwood shall provide Customer with aggregated, non-identifiable analytics derived from system-level telemetry. Aggregated exports shall not contain raw request data or model outputs, and shall enforce a minimum cohort size of 50 to reduce re-identification risk. Redwood shall maintain a documented subprocessor allowlist for the Services and provide Customer with 30 days' notice prior to onboarding any new subprocessor; Redwood reserves the right to object to additions that fail to meet security or compliance requirements."

Operational notes: Product will need a scoped commit to implement cohort enforcement and noise options prior to the first export. If VitalBridge needs exports in the current quarter, we can offer a controlled pilot with manual gating and extra logging.

Attachment: product_implementation_notes.md (text)

—Dev
Staff Product Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com
To: Tom Li <tom.li@vitalbridge.com>
Cc: Legal - VitalBridge <legal@vitalbridge.com>, olga_petrov@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: analytics carve-out and subprocessor list

Tom —

Thanks again for the redline. Per Security/Product review, attached is our proposed compromise language and an implementation plan for a pilot export (see product_implementation_notes.md). Key points: 

- Redwood agrees to a narrow analytics carve-out that permits aggregated, non-identifiable exports as long as the export meets a minimum cohort threshold of 50 and excludes any raw request text or model outputs.
- Redwood will maintain a documented subprocessor allowlist and provide 30 days' notice before onboarding new analytics partners; additions are subject to Redwood's security review.
- We can run a controlled pilot this quarter with manual gating while Product implements cohort-enforcement and optional noise injection (2–3 sprints).

If VitalBridge agrees to the attached language, please confirm and we will circulate the final DPA for signature (we can push the DocuSign session link once everything is finalized).

Proposed next step: VitalBridge confirm by EOD Wed and Legal exchange a final DPA; if accepted we'll schedule a 30-min ops/engineering sync to align pilot scope.

Thanks,
Maya
Director, Partnerships & GTM
Redwood Inference

Attachments: VB_DPA_v3_redline.pdf (pdf), product_implementation_notes.md (text)
